package cmd

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/Rivil/dross/internal/forge"
	"github.com/Rivil/dross/internal/verify"
)

// The must-trip fixture: a board issue body composed out of a Recorded field.
//
// leg is a verify.LegSummary, whose Error is declared Recorded — it holds the
// mutation adapter's failure record. Rendering it into an issue body is exactly
// what c-6 forbids, and it is written here as a fixture rather than inferred
// from the live tree so the scan is calibrated on a written-down answer.
func leakyBoardBody(client forge.Client, leg verify.LegSummary) error {
	_, err := client.CreateIssue(forge.IssueInput{
		Title: "leg failed",
		Body:  fmt.Sprintf("The %s leg failed:\n\n%s\n", leg.Tool, leg.Error),
	})
	return err
}

// The must-NOT-trip sibling: the same sink rendering a Renderable field.
// Finding.Text is derived from a record whose own text is already scrubbed
// (spec decision renderable_derivation), so a composer may print it.
func cleanBoardBody(client forge.Client, f verify.Finding) error {
	_, err := client.CreateIssue(forge.IssueInput{
		Title: "finding",
		Body:  fmt.Sprintf("- **%s**: %s\n", f.Severity, f.Text),
	})
	return err
}

// The other must-NOT-trip shape: err.Error() is a METHOD CALL, not a read of a
// declared field, and it appears in ordinary code everywhere.
func errorMethodIsNotAFieldRead(client forge.Client, err error) error {
	_, e := client.CreateIssue(forge.IssueInput{
		Title: "oops",
		Body:  fmt.Sprintf("failed: %v\n", err.Error()),
	})
	return e
}
